questions.stem: What is the name of the period when the bright portion of the Moon increases?
questions.solution: The period when the bright portion of the Moon increases is called the waxing period. The correct answer is 'Waxing period'. The other options are incorrect because the waning period is when the bright portion decreases, and new and full moons are specific phases, not periods.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to define a month in the lunar calendar?
choices: The time it takes for the Earth to complete one full rotation on its axis.
The time it takes for the Earth to complete one full revolution around the Sun.
The time it takes for the Moon to complete one full cycle of phases.
The time it takes for the stars to return to their original position at sunset.
questions.solution: In the lunar calendar, a month is defined by the time it takes for the Moon to complete one full cycle of phases, which is about 29.5 days. The other options are incorrect because the Earth's rotation defines a day, its revolution defines a year, and the stars' position is related to the sidereal year.

questions.stem: If a person observes the Moon at sunrise on a day following a full Moon, where will the Moon be in the sky relative to the Sun?
questions.solution: After a full Moon, the Moon starts to move closer to the Sun in the sky during the waning period. The correct answer is 'Closer to the Sun'. The other options are incorrect because the Moon is not farther from the Sun, not exactly where the Sun is, and is visible at sunrise in the western direction.

questions.stem: If the Moon is in a position where the illuminated part is less than half, which phase is it in?
questions.solution: If the Moon's illuminated part is less than half, it is in the crescent phase. This occurs when the Moon is positioned such that only a small portion of its surface is lit from the Sun's perspective. The New Moon has no illuminated part, the Full Moon has the entire surface illuminated, and the Gibbous Phase has more than half illuminated, making them incorrect.

hi.stem: यदि चाँद की स्थिति ऐसी हो कि उसका उज्ज्वल भाग आधे से कम हो, तो वह कौन-से चरण में होगा?
hi.solution: यदि चाँद का उज्ज्वल भाग आधे से कम हो, तो वह क्रेस्सेंट चरण में होता है। यह तब होता है जब चाँद की स्थिति ऐसी होती है कि सूर्य के दृष्टिकोण से इसकी सतह का केवल छोटा भाग ही उज्ज्वल होता है। न्यू मून में कोई उज्ज्वल भाग नहीं होता है, फुल मून में सतह का पूरा भाग उज्ज्वल होता है, और जिब्बस चरण में आधे से अधिक भाग उज्ज्वल होता है, इसलिए ये गलत हैं।

questions.stem: Which of the following festivals is celebrated on the full Moon of Vaisakha?
questions.solution: Buddha Purnima is celebrated on the full Moon of Vaisakha, which is a specific lunar event. Holi is associated with the spring equinox, Eid-ul-Fitr follows the Islamic lunar calendar's new moon, and Diwali is linked to the new moon in the month of Kartika.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why the Moon appears to move slowly across the sky compared to the Sun?
choices: The Moon is much farther from the Earth than the Sun

questions.stem: Why is the Gregorian calendar adjusted by adding a leap day every four years?
choices: To match the time it takes for the Earth to complete one full rotation on its axis.
To match the time it takes for the Earth to complete one full revolution around the Sun.
To match the time it takes for the Moon to complete one full cycle of phases.
To match the time it takes for the stars to return to their original position at sunset.
questions.solution: The Gregorian calendar is adjusted by adding a leap day every four years to account for the extra quarter of a day the Earth takes to complete one revolution around the Sun. The other options are incorrect because the Earth's rotation is the basis for the solar day, the Moon's phase cycle is not related to the calendar year, and the stars' position is related to the sidereal year, not the Gregorian calendar.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for the Sun rising in different directions during different times of the year?
choices: The Earth rotates on its axis
The Earth revolves around the Sun
The Sun moves in a circular orbit
questions.solution: The Earth's axis being tilted causes the Sun to rise in different directions throughout the year because it changes the angle at which sunlight reaches different parts of the Earth. The idea that the Sun moves in a circular orbit is incorrect because the Sun remains relatively stationary in our solar system.

questions.stem: What causes the dates of festivals based on the sidereal calendar to shift over time?
choices: The rotation of the Earth on its axis
The wobble of the Earth’s axis
The distance between the Earth and the Moon
questions.solution: The wobble of the Earth’s axis, known as precession, causes the dates of festivals based on the sidereal calendar to shift over time. The rotation of the Earth, distance between Earth and Moon, and movement of the Sun do not affect the long-term alignment of the calendar with the stars.

questions.stem: Why is the full Moon day called Purnima?
choices: Because the Moon is completely visible
Because the Moon is closest to Earth
Because the Moon is in a new phase
Because the Moon is in a waning phase
questions.solution: The correct option is because the Moon is completely visible, as this occurs when the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, making the entire face of the Moon illuminated. The Moon being closest to Earth relates to a supermoon, not Purnima. A new phase means the Moon is not visible, which contradicts the idea of a full Moon. A waning phase means the Moon is decreasing in visibility, which is the opposite of a full Moon.

questions.stem: A student observes the Moon from Earth and notices that only a part of it is illuminated. What is the reason for this observation?
choices: The Moon does not emit light of its own
The Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon
The Moon's position relative to the Earth and Sun changes
The Moon's surface is not reflective
questions.solution: The phases of the Moon occur because we see different parts of the illuminated portion of the Moon as it moves around the Earth. The Moon does not emit its own light, but it reflects sunlight. The Earth's shadow does not cause the phases, as the Moon is not in Earth's shadow during most of its cycle. The Moon's surface is reflective, which is why we can see it. The correct answer is that the Moon's position relative to the Earth and Sun changes.

questions.stem: A student observes the shadow of a stick every minute from 11:00 a.m. to 1:10 p.m. and records the time when the shadow is shortest. What can the student conclude about the Sun's position?
choices: The Sun is at its highest point in the sky
The Sun is about to set
The Sun is in the west
The Sun is in the east
questions.solution: The Sun is at its highest point in the sky because the shadow is shortest when the Sun is directly overhead. The Sun is not about to set, as this would occur later in the day. The Sun is not in the west or east at this time, as those positions correspond to sunrise and sunset, not midday.

questions.stem: If the Moon is getting farther away from the Earth and slower in its revolution, what will happen to the frequency of intercalary months in luni-solar calendars?
questions.solution: As the Moon moves farther away and its revolution slows, the length of the lunar month increases, making it less likely to fall out of sync with the solar year. This means fewer intercalary months would be needed to maintain alignment. The other options are incorrect because they do not reflect the relationship between the Moon's orbital changes and calendar adjustments.

questions.stem: If the Moon's orbit were not tilted with respect to Earth's orbit, what would happen to lunar and solar eclipses?
choices: They would not occur at all
questions.solution: The correct answer is that they would occur every month. The Moon's tilted orbit prevents eclipses from happening every month.
